summary: Passes DAT data through unchanged, giving generated networks a stable reference point while upstream DAT chains are edited or extended.

key_params.name: language
key_params.note: Use input or node script language for DAT editing behavior

key_params.name: extension
key_params.note: Choose the edit/view file extension exposed to external editors

key_params.name: customext
key_params.note: Custom extension used when Extension is set to Custom Extension

key_params.name: wordwrap
key_params.note: Control node-viewer word wrapping without changing DAT data

common_gotchas: The Null DAT has no operator-specific data parameters; it is an instance of the DAT connected to its input.
Use it as the stable output reference for generated DAT chains, not as a table generator.
Common page language, extension, and word wrap settings affect editing/display behavior rather than the table or text payload.
If the input is removed, downstream references may point at an empty or stale endpoint depending on the surrounding network.
key_concepts: Passes DAT input through as a terminal or organizational DAT node.
Null DAT is commonly used as a stable named output for text or table chains.
The operator-specific surface is intentionally sparse and mostly Common DAT parameters.
Common DAT settings still control language, editor extension, custom extension, and word wrap.
